idee_recherchee.texte: Einstein's general relativity describes gravity as the curvature of spacetime caused by mass and energy, where massive objects like stars and black holes bend the fabric around them and other objects follow those curved paths.

titre_video: Scientists Are Freaking Out Over Space Time (It's Not Real)
titre: Comment les astronomes localisent l'horizon des événements
resume: Although black holes emit or reflect no light, astronomers can see where the event horizon is because objects pulled in appear to freeze in time just before it, due to gravity's effect on time. Supermassive black holes that consumed many stars therefore appear to have objects endlessly circling the horizon even after falling in.
texte: Even though black holes themselves don't emit or reflect any light, astronomers [music] can see where the event horizon is. This is because any object that's pulled into a black hole will seem [music] to freeze in time just before the event horizon due to gravity's effect on relativistic time. What this means is that supermassive black holes that have consumed hundreds of thousands or millions of stars appear to have objects endlessly circling the event horizon, even if they've already fallen into the singularity as time seems to stop due to the immense gravity at the center of the black hole.
